title: Why Does the Ocean Have Waves?
mainIdea: Ocean waves are created by different natural forces such as wind, storms, earthquakes, and gravity.

pages.text: The ocean is always moving because waves carry energy through the water.

question.text: What is the topic of the passage?

pages.text: Most waves are created when wind blows across the surface of the ocean.

question.text: What is the most common cause of waves?

pages.text: Strong storms can create dangerous waves called storm surges. Earthquakes and volcanoes can create tsunamis.

question.text: What problem can severe weather cause?

pages.text: Earthquakes, landslides, and volcanic eruptions can quickly move large amounts of water and create tsunamis.
The sun and moon create tides through their gravitational pull. Together, these forces keep the ocean moving.

question.text: What happens in the end of the explanation?
options: Different forces work together to create waves and tides

elements.correct: To move energy across the water
distractors: To carry fish across the ocean
To push ships toward the shore

elements.correct: Different forces create different kinds of waves
distractors: Only the wind can create ocean waves

elements.correct: Waves form from wind, storms, and earthquakes
distractors: Waves form only when boats pass by
Waves form when clouds touch the water
